performance.status: MEASURED -- full canonical history, isolated single-engine run, 355696 bars
performance.latency_vs_live_budget_note: one new M15 bar arrives every 900 seconds live; measured latency is roughly 5 orders of magnitude below that budget at every percentile including the max outlier -- not a practical concern
performance.restart_serialization_growth_finding: grows with TOTAL BARS PROCESSED (~4 bytes/bar), not with active registry occupancy (which stayed at 1-2 concurrent candidates throughout this stretch). Root-caused to Registry._dead (range_semantic_v4_3.py, a documented never-reuse-a-dead-id contract) and _awaiting_role (a dict of full structure snapshots, cleared only when a specific later CONTINUATION-born candidate references the exact id AND reaches full confirmation -- a narrow condition most terminated candidates never satisfy). BOTH mechanisms exist verbatim in range_semantic_v4_3.py and range_semantic_v4_4.py -- inherited, not introduced by this mandate -- and were never previously measurable at scale because v4.4's single-candidate regime creates far fewer total lifetime candidates (187 confirmed episodes) over the same period than vNext's multi-candidate design (12813 macro-depth births alone). Practically negligible at the measured rate (~140 KB/year, low single-digit MB over decades) and does NOT affect the ACTIVE registry bound (proven bounded: max 4 observed, hard cap 16) that mandate section 20 actually gates on. NOT fixed in this mandate -- both mechanisms live in shared v4.3 infrastructure outside this mandate's authorized scope (section 17) -- flagged as a disclosed limitation (research report section 14, item 7) and a well-scoped candidate for a future, separately-authorized mandate applicable to the entire RANGE lineage.
